newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 20.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 20.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING, MARKETING & MEDIA:
HAMBURG - The power struggle over pay-TV station Premiere has escalated, with minority shareholder Leo Kirch (25 percent) calling for chief executive Bernd Kundrun to be replaced. (Der Spiegel)

MUNICH - The doomsday mood at private channel RTL2 is completely unjustified, says Munich film seller Herbert Kloiber, who owns a third of the station. RTL2 will remain independent for the next three to five years and stay in Munich, Kloiber says, opposing the planned RTL network. (Sueddeutsche Zeitung)
BONN - Deutsche Telecom AG says its plans to increase the fees it charges television companies for use of its cable network and will meet representatives of its main customers in Bonn.
(Reuter)

BONN - Munich-based car rental company Sixt AG has boosted its advertising budget for 1997 to 27 million marks ($16 million) from 20 million marks in the previous year. Chief executive Erich Sixt says it represents the highest ad budget in the industry, with the next-closest competitor spending far less on ads. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - So-called "Business TV", television programming produced by companies to train, inform and motivate employees, is catching on in Germany. Companies that use Business TV say they want to also reach partners and customers with it and cut travel costs. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

STUTTGART - Daimler-Benz AG says it plans to grow an average of eight percent per year until 1999, boosting company turnover during this time period to nearly 135 billion marks, reports the employee magazine "Headline". (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Deutsche Bank AG's new chief executive Rolf Breuer is quoted as saying he plans to reduce the bank's industrial holdings in German companies in a bid to achieve a balance between its domestic and international holldings. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Deutsche BA, which is 49-percent owned by British Airways Plc, says its revenue rose by 5.7 percent to 520 million marks in the business year to March 31, 1997 while passenger numbers rose 6.8 percent to 2.2 million. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

FRANKFURT - Dr. Joerg Pfisterer has been named marketing director of Ford Werke AG in Cologne, effective July 1. Pfisterer replaces Duncan Rooke, who will become Ford's European sales director on the same date. (Horizont)
WALLDORF - Wolfgang Kraus will begin on July 1 as board vice chairman of retail group Kaufhof AG of Cologne. Kraus will be responsible for sales, marketing and textile purchases. (Kress)

FRANKFURT - Wolfgang Koenig has been selected as director of the Healthcare Connection, launched by the Frankfurt ad agency of Saatchi & Saatchi. The new unit will officially open on July 1. (Horizont)
WALLDORF - Fridolin Luchsinger has started as the director of the department Ringier Communication at publishing house Ringier AG in Zurich, serving as press spokesman. (Kress)
Deborah Cole, Berlin Newsroom, 49-30-203-98114
